title: Keep an alert's recipients as they were when it was sent

blocks.text: The on-call tool pages engineers through `Alert`. Its scheduler keeps the current rotation in one `String[]`, passes it to every alert it sends, and writes the next week's names into the same array each Monday. Since the last release, three things have gone wrong: last week's alerts in the history show this week's engineers, the rotation itself comes back in a different order after an alert is sent, and on a fresh install, where no rotation has been set up yet, the first alert crashed the scheduler.
`Alert` already renders a page. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/Alert.java`:

items: `to(title, recipients...)`: the alert for those recipients, which the pager lists in alphabetical order.

blocks.text: When you're done, an alert lists the people it was created for, whatever the scheduler does to its array afterwards, the scheduler's array is left as it was, and an alert sent before any rotation exists goes to nobody. About five lines in total.

cases.says: an alert keeps its title and lists the recipients it was given in alphabetical order, and an alert with none lists none
a null array of recipients gives an alert with no recipients instead of an exception
creating an alert leaves the order of the caller's array as it was
when the caller later writes other names into the array it passed, the alert already created keeps its recipients

origin.section: A Varargs Parameter Is an Array: the Caller Can Pass Its Own, or null

concepts: A null argument to a varargs parameter arrives as a null array, not as an array holding one null, so the method must decide what a null array means.
An array passed to a varargs parameter becomes the parameter itself, so the method shares the caller's array: sorting it or keeping it reaches the caller.
